title: Implement event-time bucketing and source-weighting to prevent backfill-induced spikes in per-model usage breakdowns
creator: Ava Chen
description: Console per-model breakdown charts are intermittently showing large, short-lived spikes after late/backfilled ingestion. Root cause investigation shows we aggregate using ingestion_time windowing and then apply a sliding smoothing algorithm in the frontend which treats late-arriving events as current, causing apparent model shifts and metric 'wash-out'. This confuses customers and increases support tickets and billing disputes. This ticket implements an event-time-first aggregation strategy plus per-source weighting and explicit backfill visibility to prevent misattribution and reduce noise in charts.
acceptance_criteria: Console per-model daily breakdowns maintain <= 2% relative change in stable windows after simulated backfill vs a golden baseline
Late-arrival/backfill events are visible in the UI with a clear visual marker and a tooltip explaining event_time vs ingestion_time
Backend aggregation stores both event_time_rollup and ingestion_time_rollup for every time bucket and supports queries that prefer event_time_rollup by default
Automatic detection flags a backfill window when buffered/lateness exceeds watermark threshold and increments a backfill_rate metric
No increase in token-count double-counting incidents after rollouts (verified by synthetic regression tests)
proposed_solution: Add/ensure event_time and source_id fields on ingestion schema (kafka message contract) and populate at emitters
Switch streaming aggregator (kstream/beam) to event-time tumbling windows with watermarking and late-event handlers rather than ingestion-time bucketing
Persist both event_time_rollup and ingestion_time_rollup in rollup store (immutable writes with idempotency keys) so historical queries can choose attribution mode

Introduce a small source-weighting heuristic: when a model token count for the same event appears in multiple sources due to replays, weight by earliest source_timestamp and a trust-score to reduce duplicates

Add a backfill flag on buckets when events arrive beyond watermark and surface that flag to Console via API; Console should render an overlay and optionally exclude flagged buckets from default smoothing
Add a lightweight reprocess tool for limited windows that writes to rollup store using non-destructive upserts and produces a reconciliation report
Expose observability metrics: late_event_fraction, backfill_rate, model_delta_24h, and ingestion_vs_event_count_ratio for alerting
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the new event-time aggregation in streaming pipeline (off by default).
Canary: enable for internal orgs and 5% of production traffic for 48 hours; monitor backfill_rate and per-model-delta metrics.
After canary success, enable for all organizations but keep Console UI behind an opt-in toggle for 1 week to collect UX feedback.
Schedule controlled reprocess for affected historical windows during a low-traffic maintenance window; gradually expand reprocessing scope if reconciliation metrics look good.
Full enablement and removal of old ingestion-time defaults after 4 weeks of stable telemetry and sign-off from PM and Reliability
testing_notes: Create synthetic stream jobs that emit normal, delayed (2h-48h), and burst backfill events; validate rollups against a golden dataset
Add unit tests for watermark and late-event handlers to ensure deterministic bucketing
Integration tests that simulate duplicate events across sources and verify source-weighting reduces overcounting
QA checklist: verify Console shows backfill overlay, verify API returns event_time_rollup/ingestion_time_rollup, validate edge-case windows with zero-latency and extreme-lateness
Run cost estimate for reprocessing 30 days of high-volume shards and include fallback stop-if-cost-exceeds guard
observability_changes: New metrics: usage.backfill_rate, usage.late_event_fraction, usage.model_delta_24h, usage.ingest_vs_event_ratio
Dashboards: Backfill Overview (global), Per-Model Backfill Impact (top 50 models), Reprocess Job Health
Alerts: page if backfill_rate > 0.5% AND model_delta_24h > 5% for > 15m; ticket if reprocess failure rate > 2%
Tracing: add span tagging in aggregator for 'window_assigned' and 'late_event_handler' to track latency/distribution
